answer: Each identity registers a forge heat, locks a 60-credit bond, casts a hollow sleeve and presses it into a velvet pad whose impression is filed as consumed. An auditor recomputes wall thickness from its diameters and checks the velvet impression against the heat number; a mismatch or reused pad burns the bond. The first sleeve costs 30 credits, the kth costs 30+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5025 and 1000 fakes cost 2,527,500 plus 60,000 locked. A rented sleeve fails: its velvet impression matches another heat number. An honest operator pays 30 once and recovers the bond after a clean assay.
